thread:
janet: Quick heads-up: running the TS SDK sample with Bun fails during startup. Error: "The package "node:crypto" could not be found".
luis: Hmm, are we importing `node:crypto` anywhere unconditionally? Bun has its own node-compat layer but it isn't 1:1.
arya: Found it in utils/sign.ts: `import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'`. We added that to be explicit for Node ESM, but it breaks Bun and likely Deno.
janet: Also types complain in Deno: `Cannot find name 'Buffer'`. Our d.ts references Buffer in a few helper types.
ci-bot: @janet opened issue #1499 - "SDK runtime assumptions: node builtins + Buffer in types"; added label devex/deno-bun.
luis: Proposed fixes: 1) avoid `node:` specifier in source, or gate via build aliases; 2) runtime detection for webcrypto vs node crypto; 3) replace Buffer-based types with Uint8Array in public API types, keep internal narrow helpers that accept Buffer | Uint8Array.
arya: For imports we can use conditional exports in package.json so `import from 'redwood'` in Deno/Bun resolves to dist/esm/browser.js while Node gets dist/cjs or dist/esm/node.js. But Deno ignores package.json exports and uses specifier imports. We should publish a top-level `deno` entrypoint or examples that use explicit URL imports.
janet: Example failing snippet I used: ```ts
// example-deno.ts
import { signRequest } from 'redwood'
const sig = await signRequest(new TextEncoder().encode('hi'))
```
luis: Deno will try to resolve to the registry package at import time; if package.json points to CJS it'll fail. We should add a Deno example that imports from the ES module path: `import { signRequest } from 'https://cdn.example.com/redwood@1.2.3/dist/esm/mod.js'` or guide users to `import from 'redwood/dist/esm/mod.js'` when using Deno local installs.
arya: On fetch/streams: our upload helper uses `response.body.getReader()` which Deno supports on web streams, but Bun's fetch returns a Node-like stream in some versions. We need to detect `response.body?.getReader` and fallback to `.arrayBuffer()` or Node stream consumption.
janet: For HMAC signing we can implement a small abstraction: `async function hmacSha256(key, msg){ if (globalThis.crypto?.subtle) { const k = await crypto.subtle.importKey(...); return crypto.subtle.sign(...)} else { const { createHmac } = await import('crypto'); return createHmac('sha256', key).update(msg).digest() } }`
luis: Types: we should change exported signatures from `Buffer` to `Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer` and add small helper `toUint8Array` in runtime. Also ship `types-deno.d.ts` for Deno users if necessary.
ci-bot: @luis created PR draft #1502 (deno-bun-compat): adds dist/esm, types update, and runtime crypto detection. CI: added deno:stable and bun:latest matrix jobs.
arya: Suggest adding a tiny compat shim in examples: ```js
// examples/compat-shim.js
if (typeof globalThis.Buffer === 'undefined') globalThis.Buffer = { from: (b)=> new Uint8Array(b) }
if (!globalThis.crypto?.subtle && typeof globalThis.require === 'function') { const { webcrypto } = require('crypto'); globalThis.crypto = webcrypto }
```
janet: Not ideal, but helpful for partners. Also add an entry in README: "If you are running in Deno/Bun, import from 'redwood/dist/esm/mod.js' or see examples/deno.md".
luis: One more gotcha: Deno's permission model requires `--allow-env` for reading env. Our examples currently do `Deno.env.get('REDWOOD_KEY')` without comment. We should document that Deno requires extra flags and recommend env-based injection for edge usage.
arya: For CI, I'll add a smoke test: `deno run --allow-net --allow-env examples/deno/simple.ts` and `bun examples/bun/simple.ts` in the PR pipeline. If those fail, block merge.
node-deps-bot: dependency bump: bumped types/node -> 20.3.0 (may affect typings).
j anet: Thanks everyone. Let's keep this minimal: land PR with ESM builds + runtime detection first, then follow up on types and docs.
ci-bot: Added tasks to PR checklist: update README, add deno/bun examples, add smoke tests to CI.
luis: I'll rework the sign.ts to be web-first and Node fallback, push by EOD.
arya: I'll update types in a separate PR to avoid big churn.
j anet: Great. Will test PR against partner demo once merged.
